look_here_first: GREEN SPRANGLETOP: look for a usually PERENNIAL, often robust bunch with relatively broad bluish-green blades and a terminal head of about 2–15 long slender branches, frequently widely spreading or gently drooping. Branches carry spikelets mostly on ONE side. Then examine ONE mature 4–12 mm spikelet at 10–20×: commonly 4–13 florets (count inside one spikelet), with fairly blunt or NOTCHED, generally awnless or minutely pointed lemmas ~3.5–5 mm long. At the blade–sheath junction verify a SHORT MEMBRANOUS ligule with a fringed margin; in lower sheaths look for optional HIDDEN self-pollinating (cleistogamous) flowers. A flowering-head photo alone cannot prove florets, notches, ligule or hidden heads.

best_field_traits: PERENNIAL: typically stout bunchgrass with a lasting tough base, sometimes locally producing basal tillers; do not infer a root system from a cut stem.

PANICLE BRANCHES: usually about 2–15 slender, long, often widely spreading or nodding branches arranged along a main flowering axis; spikelets on mostly ONE side (secund). Inflorescence branch count is supporting, not uniquely diagnostic.
SPIKELETS: about 4–12 mm long, 4–13 florets PER INDIVIDUAL SPIKELET; count florets on the rachilla, not spikelets on different branches. Fertile florets may spread widely at maturity.
LEMMA: usually ~3.5–5 mm long, 3-veined, often hairy toward lower margins; tip broad, nearly square/obtuse to shallowly notched, awnless or with a tiny mucro, NOT a long threeawn bristle.
LIGULE: actual short membranous inside blade/sheath junction with a fringed/ciliate upper edge; genus treatment typically 0.5–1.5 mm, Flora of North America sometimes 1–2 mm.

SECONDARY HEADS: may produce cleistogamous (closed, self-pollinating) panicles enclosed LOW in leaf sheaths. Seeing one strongly supports ID; failing to find one on a single stalk does not rule species out.
Older names LEPTOCHLOA DUBIA / DIPLACHNE DUBIA are synonyms for the same plant. State-wide nativity or taxonomic flags were NOT newly audited in this visual upgrade.
what_to_photograph_for_confirmation: FULL HABIT: same individual photographed from tough perennial crown (with any basal tillers) to flowering head; add a centimeter ruler and note if stolons are present.
PANICLE: entire 2–15 branch flowering head with at least one branch showing its mostly one-sided spikelet attachment and where each branch arises along the main axis.
SPIKELET 10–20×: mm ruler beside an intact 4–12 mm spikelet, glumes and rachilla visible so 4–13 FLORETS can be individually counted.
LEMMA 20×: separate a mature 3.5–5 mm lemma and show its approximately flat/square, often shallowly two-notched tip, hair placement and any tiny mucro; do not claim a long awn.
TRUE COLLAR: unfold a blade and measure membranous ligule with finely fringed apex, showing the actual blade/sheath junction (2013 treatment 0.5–1.5 mm; some regional accounts 1–2 mm).
LOW SHEATHS: on the same plant, document an enclosed cleistogamous flowering head when present; absence in one sheath is not a negative ID.
MATCHED COMPARISON: Dinebra panicea subsp. mucronata full annual plant plus 2–4 mm 2–4-flowered mature spikelet, both shot at the same scale as Disakisperma.
crew_field_check: Trace a WHOLE rooted individual, not just a detached panicle: green sprangletop normally perennial, annual Dinebra has much finer panicle branches.
Observe the side of a mature flowering branch where spikelets line up. Under magnification, count individual florets inside ONE measured mature spikelet.
Look closely for broad square/obtuse often NOTCHED lemma tip and a genuinely fringed membranous ligule, and optionally a hidden secondary flowering head in a lower sheath.

Compare Dinebra on spikelet LENGTH and floret COUNT as well as habit: Disakisperma 4–12 mm and 4–13 florets, Dinebra commonly ~2–4 mm and 2–4 florets; counts can overlap, so don't decide from four alone.
Two new credited Commons photos show the real species from west Texas but do not demonstrate invisible microscopic anatomy; only mark what is actually visible.

comparisons.key_distinctions: DINEBRA PANICEA subsp. MUCRONATA (mucronate sprangletop): generally a slender ANNUAL with MANY fine ascending branches, tiny ~2–4 mm spikelets with typically 2–4 florets and a much smaller lemma; Green sprangletop is a usually larger PERENNIAL with about 2–15 often widely spreading branches and ~4–12 mm spikelets with 4–13 florets. Both may bear four-flowered spikelets: measure the actual mature spikelet AND inspect rooted habit before deciding. DIPLACHNE FUSCA (bearded sprangletop) can also have long spreading branches; its ligule tends to be much longer and pointed (often ~2–8 mm), and lemma tip shape differs, so confirm with a microscope. Old Leptochloa dubia and Diplachne dubia refer to the same green sprangletop taxon, not new cards. Do not mistake a single branch of the panicle for a whole spikelet.

measured_diagnostic_key.habit: Mostly perennial tufted or occasionally stoloniferous; document rooted crown rather than assuming perennial from a clipped flowering stem.
measured_diagnostic_key.terminal_panicle_cm: 10–45 long, 3–25 wide; raceme-like unilateral branches commonly 5–15
measured_diagnostic_key.spikelets_mm: 4–12, 4–13 florets, usually nearly sessile on unilateral branches
measured_diagnostic_key.lemma_mm: 3.5–5.0, usually 3-veined, often hairy on margins/below, apex sometimes shallowly bifid, awnless or minutely mucronate
measured_diagnostic_key.cleistogamy: Additional closed-flowering spikelets may be hidden in LOWER leaf sheaths; photograph on the same plant without claiming absence when not found.

look_alike_field_key.compare: Generally annual with 2–4(–5) florets per much smaller 2–4 mm spikelet and lemma about 0.9–1.7 mm in regional descriptions. Check rooted annual base, glumes, and true floret count; don't infer species from thin one-sided branches alone.
Require mature lemma length, floret count, ligule, and hidden lower-sheath inflorescences; retain Disakisperma sp. if structures are missing.

same_plant_photo_sequence: FULL HABIT: same individual photographed from tough perennial crown (with any basal tillers) to flowering head; add a centimeter ruler and note if stolons are present.
PANICLE: entire 2–15 branch flowering head with at least one branch showing its mostly one-sided spikelet attachment and where each branch arises along the main axis.
SPIKELET 10–20×: mm ruler beside an intact 4–12 mm spikelet, glumes and rachilla visible so 4–13 FLORETS can be individually counted.
LEMMA 20×: separate a mature 3.5–5 mm lemma and show its approximately flat/square, often shallowly two-notched tip, hair placement and any tiny mucro; do not claim a long awn.
TRUE COLLAR: unfold a blade and measure membranous ligule with finely fringed apex, showing the actual blade/sheath junction (2013 treatment 0.5–1.5 mm; some regional accounts 1–2 mm).
LOW SHEATHS: on the same plant, document an enclosed cleistogamous flowering head when present; absence in one sheath is not a negative ID.
MATCHED COMPARISON: Dinebra panicea subsp. mucronata full annual plant plus 2–4 mm 2–4-flowered mature spikelet, both shot at the same scale as Disakisperma.
field_id_finish_pass.annotation_gaps: Existing provisional photograph does not verify ligule, glume dimensions, individual florets, lemma tip or enclosed lower-sheath flowers. Keep existing arrows; do not place new structure-specific arrows until pixels and scale are verified.
field_id_finish_pass.public_ready_criteria: FIELD_READY_PHOTO_GAPS until a species-vouchered, publicly permitted same-plant series shows base, collar, mature spikelet/florets and lemma; verify source/creator/license, photo bytes, image-level arrow targets, and Pages display separately.
handoff: NEEDS_PUBLIC_PHOTO: publicly permitted macro of collar, dissected mature spikelet and hidden lower-sheath head (if present). Existing CC BY-NC image requires noncommercial site-use check.
NEEDS_SITE_QA: ensure measurements render, existing arrows match real pixels, attribution and rights filter survive site build; do not claim live deployment.
measured_key_sources: Peterson et al., Systematics of Disakisperma, PhytoKeys 26 (2013), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3817421/ (species treatment and genus ligule).

lane4_matt_lavin_local_archive_20261023.last_mile: Measured actual same-source rootstock, 1mm ligule, mature glume/lemma and concealed lower-sheath florets

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 01 · LOOK HERE FIRST
field_id_short_tiles.short: Perennial bunch; ~2–15 long, often spreading one-sided branches
field_id_short_tiles.details: Follow the whole rooted plant from a persistent base to its flowering head. Green sprangletop typically bears ~2–15 long raceme-like branches, often spreading or drooping, with spikelets mostly aligned on ONE side. A branch is not a spikelet. Panels 1–3 and 7 show real source-determined head or habit, but no single image yet proves all diagnostic parts of one Hays specimen.
field_id_short_tiles.status: FIELD-READY HEAD CUE; SAME-PLANT ROOTED HABIT GAP

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 02 · OPEN THE TRUE LEAF COLLAR
field_id_short_tiles.short: Short ~0.5–1.5 mm membranous ligule with fringed edge
field_id_short_tiles.details: At the inner blade–sheath junction, expose the true short membrane and distinguish its ciliate margin from separate sheath hairs. Regional sources sometimes give 1–2 mm; do not turn source variation into a false cutoff. Panel 4 is a real photographed collar region, but a 1-mm ruler and verified membrane-tip arrow are still required.

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 03 · COUNT FLORETS INSIDE ONE SPIKELET
field_id_short_tiles.details: At 10–20× isolate ONE mature spikelet on its one-sided branch. Count individual florets along the rachilla, not separate spikelets along the branch. Existing attached and opened flowering-unit photos (panels 5–6 and 9–12) support the anatomy concept, but only an intact mature spikelet beside a 1-mm ruler can confirm length and floret count.

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 04 · EXPOSE THE TWO BASAL GLUMES
field_id_short_tiles.short: Lower ~2.3–4.8 mm; upper ~3.3–6 mm in published key
field_id_short_tiles.details: Gently dissect a mature spikelet and distinguish the two basal glumes from the successive lemmas. Existing treatments give lower glume (1.6–)2.3–4.8 mm and upper glume ~3.3–6 mm; these are published ranges, not measurements from the current gallery. Show the attachment and both glumes against a 1-mm ruler before adding any structure-level arrow.

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 05 · EXAMINE THE BLUNT LEMMA AND LOW SHEATHS
field_id_short_tiles.short: Lemma ~3.5–5 mm, 3-veined, blunt/notched; no long awn
field_id_short_tiles.details: At 20× expose a mature fertile lemma, commonly ~3.5–5 mm and three-veined, with a broad nearly square or shallowly notched tip and at most a minute mucro rather than a long awn. Panel 5 shows real teased flowering parts but does not independently calibrate the tip. Optional closed self-pollinating heads may hide in lower sheaths; their absence from one culm is not evidence against this species.
field_id_short_tiles.status: NEEDS_PUBLIC_PHOTO — MEASURED LEMMA TIP AND OPTIONAL SHEATH HEAD

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 06 · SEPARATE MUCRONATE SPRANGLETOP
field_id_short_tiles.short: Larger usually perennial spikelets vs Dinebra's small annual units
field_id_short_tiles.details: Panel 13 is Dinebra panicea subsp. mucronata, a DIFFERENT canonical taxon under separate taxonomy/photo review; do not treat a brachiata-complex photo as a confirmed mucronata specimen. Dinebra is generally a finer-branched annual with ~2–4 mm, ~2–4-flowered spikelets; green sprangletop is typically perennial with ~4–12 mm, ~4–13-flowered spikelets. Four florets can overlap, so measure spikelets and check rooted habit and glumes. Diplachne fusca may have a longer ~2–8 mm ligule; confirm mature lemma shape rather than branch spread alone.
field_id_short_tiles.status: FIELD-READY DIFFERENTIAL; SAME-SCALE LOCAL ANATOMY MISSING

grass_species_finalization_20261025.scope: Six concise existing-species Central Texas field-ID tiles added; no images, arrows, taxonomy, nativity, genus, family, website or Pages edits.
grass_species_finalization_20261025.measured_source_notes: Published ranges (not direct measurements of current JPEGs): mostly perennial; ~2–15 raceme-like branches; ~4–12 mm spikelets with ~4–13 florets; lower glume (1.6–)2.3–4.8 mm, upper glume ~3.3–6 mm; fertile lemma ~3.5–5 mm, usually three-veined, blunt/notched, awnless or minutely mucronate; short ciliate membranous ligule ~0.5–1.5 mm (some treatments 1–2 mm).
NEEDS_PUBLIC_PHOTO: Taxon-verified same-plant rooted perennial crown, collar and entire branching flowering head with centimeter ruler.
Inner blade–sheath junction at 10–20× with true ~0.5–1.5 mm fringed membranous ligule and 1-mm ruler; inspect existing panel 4 before new arrow.
One mature ~4–12 mm spikelet with 4–13 florets individually distinguishable on the rachilla and 1-mm scale.
Both glumes isolated at the same scale; separate ~3.5–5 mm three-veined lemma showing broad/notched apex and any minute mucro.
Optional lower-sheath closed flowering head documented on the same specimen if present, and matched voucher-verified Dinebra mucronata reproductive comparison.
NEEDS_SITE_QA: Preserve all existing Bob Harms credited educational-use (not CC), Jim Conrad public-domain, Matt Lavin CC BY-SA 2.0 and original CC BY-NC photograph records and source/license distinctions.
Check existing broad arrows and anatomy panels against real archived JPEG pixels; no unseen ligule-tip, glume, lemma or enclosed-head arrow.
Confirm six short tiles and public-rights-filtered panels render on ordinary public Visual Learner; no site or Pages changes in this lane.
grass_species_finalization_20261025.public_ready_criteria: Keep FIELD_READY_PHOTO_GAPS until an exact-taxon measured same-plant series shows rooted growth, true ligule, intact mature spikelet, separate glumes and lemma, with any comparison taxa independently verified; then inspect annotation pixels and rights-filtered public rendering.
